Prehistory field school

A three-day field school in survey, stone tools, rock art and megaliths

On request

Arranged for your group. Send your preferred dates, group size and starting point. We prepare a day-by-day itinerary and a quotation, and revise both until they suit you. The suggested group size is a guide, not a requirement.

Request on WhatsApp Request by email

No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

A field introduction to prehistory: reading the local landscape, locating and classifying stone tools, documenting rock art and megaliths, and taking samples.

Dates, location and syllabus are agreed with your institution. A day-by-day plan and a quotation are shared before you commit.

What it covers

  • Reading the local landscape
  • Finding and classifying stone tools
  • Documenting rock art and megaliths
  • Taking samples

Day by day

  1. Day 1: Reading the landscape

    Maps, geology and survey: how prehistorians decide where to look.

  2. Day 2: Stone tools

    Finding, recording and classifying stone tools, and what their scars tell us.

  3. Day 3: Rock art and megaliths

    Documenting rock art and megalithic monuments, and how samples are taken and labelled.

Days can be added, removed or reordered. The final itinerary comes with your quotation.
